cards.title: FoodShare Wisconsin (SNAP)
cards.notes: Provides food benefits to low-income households.

cards.title: Feeding America Eastern Wisconsin
cards.notes: Largest food bank in eastern Wisconsin.

cards.title: Second Harvest Foodbank of Southern Wisconsin
cards.notes: Primary food bank for Madison metro.

cards.title: Feeding America: River Bend Food Bank
cards.notes: Primary food bank for Green Bay and Fox Valley.

cards.title: WIC Wisconsin
cards.notes: Provides supplemental foods, health care referrals, and nutrition education for low-income pregnant, breastfeeding, and non-breastfeeding postpartum women, and to infants and children up to age five who are found to be at nutritional risk.

cards.title: W-2 Wisconsin Works (TANF)
cards.notes: Intensive work requirements - tiered slots from $608-$673/month. 60-month limit.

cards.title: BadgerCare+ (Wisconsin Medicaid)
cards.notes: Provides health care coverage for low-income Wisconsin residents.

cards.title: Milwaukee County Behavioral Health Division
cards.notes: Public mental health and SUD treatment, crisis services, inpatient.

cards.title: Sixteenth Street Community Health Centers
cards.notes: Comprehensive FQHC for Latino/Hispanic and low-income residents, sliding scale.

cards.title: Neighbor to Neighbor
cards.notes: FQHC sliding scale primary care including Hmong-language services.

cards.title: Wisconsin Federally Qualified Health Centers
cards.notes: Sliding scale primary, dental, behavioral health.

cards.title: Wisconsin Housing and Economic Development Authority (WHEDA)
cards.notes: HOME program, emergency rental assistance, Section 8/HCV coordination.

cards.title: Wisconsin WHEAP (Home Energy Assistance Program)
cards.notes: Heating, cooling, crisis shutoff prevention.

cards.title: Legal Aid Society of Milwaukee
cards.notes: Housing (eviction), family, benefits, DV, consumer, immigration, elder.

cards.title: Wisconsin Judicare
cards.notes: Housing, family, benefits, tribal law, ICWA.

cards.title: Legal Action of Wisconsin
cards.notes: Housing, benefits, DV, consumer.

cards.title: State Bar of Wisconsin Lawyer Referral
cards.notes: Low-cost or pro bono referrals through county bar associations.

cards.title: Wisconsin Coalition Against DV (WCADV)
cards.notes: 24/7 statewide DV hotline - crisis, shelter referral, safety planning.

cards.title: Milwaukee Women's Center / Sojourner Family Peace Center
cards.notes: Shelter, legal advocacy, transitional housing.

cards.title: Wisconsin UI
cards.notes: Unemployment insurance for workers who lost their job through no fault of their own.

cards.title: Public Service Commission of Wisconsin (PSC)
cards.notes: Winter utility shutoff protection November 1 - April 15 for low-income customers.

cards.title: Menominee Indian Tribe of Wisconsin - Social Services
cards.notes: Tribal TANF, housing, health (Menominee Indian Tribe Health Center), child welfare, elder, education.

cards.title: Ho-Chunk Nation Department of Social Services
cards.notes: Tribal TANF, housing, health, elder, education; trust land in multiple WI counties.

cards.title: Lac du Flambeau Band of Lake Superior Chippewa - Social Services
cards.notes: Tribal TANF, housing, health, elder, treaty rights services.

cards.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
cards.summary: Call or text 988 for immediate mental health crisis support. Free, confidential, 24/7. Trained counselors can help with suicidal thoughts, emotional distress, substance use, and mental health crises. Also available via chat at 988lifeline.org.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone experiencing a mental health crisis, suicidal thoughts, or emotional distress.
cards.how_to_access: Call or text 988. Chat at 988lifeline.org. For veterans, press 1 after dialing 988.

cards.title: NAMI Helpline & Support Groups
cards.summary: National Alliance on Mental Illness provides free peer support, education, and advocacy. NAMI HelpLine: 1-800-950-NAMI (6264). Family-to-Family program helps families understand mental health conditions and navigate the system.
cards.who_qualifies: Individuals with mental health conditions and their family members.
cards.how_to_access: Call 1-800-950-NAMI or text 'HELPLINE' to 62640. Find local NAMI affiliate at nami.org/find-support.

cards.title: Protection & Advocacy Organization
cards.summary: Every state has a federally mandated Protection & Advocacy (P&A) organization with legal authority to investigate abuse and neglect in psychiatric facilities. P&A organizations can enter any facility, access records, and file lawsuits. This is often the most powerful tool available for people harmed in the mental health system.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone with a disability who has experienced abuse, neglect, or rights violations in a facility.
cards.how_to_access: Find your state P&A at ndrn.org/about/ndrn-member-agencies/ or call the NDRN at 202-408-9514.

cards.title: Know Your Rights: Wisconsin Emergency Detention
cards.summary: If you are placed on an involuntary hold in WI, you have rights: the initial hold cannot exceed 72 hours without a court hearing. You have the right to an attorney at the hearing. You have the right to present evidence and call witnesses. You have the right to an independent psychiatric evaluation. You can challenge the hold at any time.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone placed on an involuntary psychiatric hold or facing commitment proceedings.
cards.how_to_access: Request to speak with the patient advocate. Ask for a copy of your patient rights. Contact your state's Protection & Advocacy organization.

cards.title: Your Right to Your Psychiatric Records
cards.summary: Under HIPAA (45 CFR § 164.524), you have the right to access your complete medical record, including psychiatric treatment records. The facility must respond within 30 days. If they deny access, you can file a complaint with HHS Office for Civil Rights. Under HIPAA § 164.526, you also have the right to request amendments to inaccurate records.
cards.who_qualifies: Any current or former psychiatric patient.
cards.how_to_access: Submit a written request to the facility's Health Information Management department. If denied, file complaint at hhs.gov/ocr.

cards.title: SAMHSA National Helpline
cards.summary: Free, confidential, 24/7 treatment referral and information service for mental health and substance use disorders. Available in English and Spanish. Provides referrals to local treatment facilities, support groups, and community-based organizations.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone seeking mental health or substance use treatment information and referrals.
